worlds.name: Earth

environment.surface: oceans and heavily developed continents

settlement.reason_founded: Human homeworld.
settlement.why_remain: Largest concentration of human population, institutions, culture and diversified industry.
settlement.character: Ancient cities coexist with immense orbital logistics infrastructure.

culture: Earth remains culturally fragmented rather than becoming a single planetary culture.
Offworld freight is routine but surface access is highly regulated.
worlds.visual_identity: Dense coastal megaregions, old urban fabric, orbital elevators/transfer infrastructure where practical, crowded skies and mature ports.

worlds.name: Luna

environment.surface: regolith, excavated industrial zones

settlement.reason_founded: Near-Earth industry, science and launch logistics.
settlement.why_remain: Low gravity and proximity to Earth make it an enduring manufacturing and transshipment location.
settlement.character: Old infrastructure repeatedly expanded rather than replaced.

worlds.visual_identity: Excavated terminals, pressure tunnels, buried habitats and industrial scars visible across worked terrain.

worlds.name: Mars

environment.surface: cold desert

settlement.reason_founded: Science, settlement ambition and local resources.
settlement.why_remain: Large established population and industrial base independent of Earth's surface constraints.
settlement.character: A mature world rather than a frontier colony.

worlds.visual_identity: Dust-muted cities, pressure districts, rail freight and generations of additions.

worlds.name: Keshar

environment.atmosphere: dense, breathable to Kesh; shared environments require conditioning
environment.surface: shallow seas, broad continental shelves and rugged uplands

settlement.reason_founded: Kesh homeworld.
settlement.why_remain: Civilizational center and enormous heavy-industrial economy.
settlement.character: Infrastructure is designed for high loads, violent weather and long service lives.

culture: Maintenance records commonly outlive owners and companies.
Foreign crews joke that Kesh buildings are engineered to survive the planet disappearing beneath them.
worlds.visual_identity: Low broad cities, enormous foundations, sea walls, gantries, pressure-rated transit and visibly massive structural members.

worlds.name: Ilos

environment.surface: deep basins, immense escarpments and vertical geology

settlement.reason_founded: Ilyan homeworld.
settlement.why_remain: Civilizational center and precision-manufacturing economy.
settlement.character: Vertical distance is inexpensive; unnecessary mass is culturally conspicuous.

culture: Architecture treats height as humans treat horizontal distance.
Imported heavy machinery is often stripped and rebuilt to remove mass.
worlds.visual_identity: Tall skeletal towers, suspended infrastructure, cliff cities, long-span bridges and lightweight transit.

worlds.name: Veyara

environment.surface: global ocean with island arcs and shallow continental seas

settlement.reason_founded: Vey homeworld.
settlement.why_remain: Civilizational center with unmatched biological and environmental industries.
settlement.character: The boundary between city, port and water-management system is often indistinct.

culture: Water is treated as inhabited space rather than an obstacle.
Dry interiors designed for visitors can feel wastefully arid to Vey.
worlds.visual_identity: Floating districts, submerged infrastructure, island industry, causeways, pumps and enormous water-processing works.

worlds.name: Orun

environment.surface: rocky terrain with extreme diurnal temperature swings
environment.habitability: native Orun biosphere; surface exposure seasonally difficult

settlement.reason_founded: Orun homeworld.
settlement.why_remain: Civilizational center whose subterranean infrastructure is effectively a second geology.
settlement.character: Cities grow by excavation and connection rather than outward surface sprawl.

culture: Mechanical spaces are ordinary social spaces.
Privacy is created deliberately when needed rather than assumed by architecture.
worlds.visual_identity: Sparse surface entrances over enormous tunnel cities, ceramic liners, heat exchangers and machinery embedded beside homes and markets.

worlds.name: Concord Prime

environment.atmosphere: breathable with routine multispecies conditioning indoors
environment.surface: temperate continents and shallow inland seas

settlement.reason_founded: Neutral meeting and exchange site during the early multispecies trade era.
settlement.why_remain: Its institutions, standards bodies, finance and route position became more valuable than its original physical resources.
settlement.character: No single species' planning assumptions dominate the built environment.

culture: Commercial signage and public facilities are deliberately multispecies.
The SCU standard is a point of local civic pride despite being mundane elsewhere.
worlds.visual_identity: Layered trade cities, standardized freight architecture, mixed habitat districts and enormous intermodal terminals.

worlds.name: Roosevelt

environment.atmosphere: breathable but cold; severe seasonal weather
environment.surface: cold mineral-rich continents, mountain belts and inland seas
environment.habitability: outdoor survival practical with climate protection

settlement.reason_founded: Accessible mineral deposits and a viable human settlement environment.
settlement.why_remain: Shipbuilding, fabrication and a mature industrial workforce.
settlement.character: Nearly every city has some relationship to fabrication, extraction or orbital construction.

culture: Independent captains treat New Houston as neutral ground between manufacturers.
Practical mixed-species engineering is valued more than design purity.
worlds.visual_identity: Snow, mines, rail freight, fabrication sheds, launch fields and orbital yards crowded with half-built commercial hulls.

worlds.name: Hesperus

environment.surface: broad plains, shallow seas and long temperate growing belts

settlement.reason_founded: Unusually favorable large-scale agriculture.
settlement.why_remain: Its food exports support several industrial systems.
settlement.character: Low population density despite enormous economic footprint.

culture: Harvest schedules affect freight pricing more than politics does.
Ports smell like soil, machinery, refrigerant and livestock rather than spacecraft.
worlds.visual_identity: Huge fields, irrigation geometry, grain elevators, cold stores, agricultural machinery and widely separated towns.

worlds.name: Iron Gate Prime

environment.atmosphere: breathable with industrial controls around major cities
environment.surface: dry rocky continents with accessible mineral provinces

settlement.reason_founded: Kesh mining colony with lower gravity than Keshar.
settlement.why_remain: Low gravity plus heavy industry made construction of enormous spacecraft economical.
settlement.character: The sky is dominated by orbital construction rather than surface prestige architecture.

culture: Large hull construction is a civic identity.
Workers from every species arrive for multi-year yard contracts.
worlds.visual_identity: Ore trains, vast casting works, orbital rings of incomplete hulls and cranes sized like buildings.

worlds.name: Carver Belt

environment.surface: metal-rich asteroids

settlement.reason_founded: Exceptionally accessible metal resources.
settlement.why_remain: Known-space industry continuously consumes its output.
settlement.character: The workplace is distributed across moving rocks rather than a planetary surface.

worlds.visual_identity: Tugs, drilling frames, refinery lights, rotating work camps and ore bags against black space.

worlds.name: Carver Habitats

environment.surface: stations and excavated asteroids

settlement.reason_founded: Housing and services for belt extraction.
settlement.why_remain: Mining economy and generations of permanent residents.
settlement.character: Everything ordinary is valuable because almost everything ordinary was shipped in.

culture: Used consumer goods retain value unusually long.
Freight arrivals are visible social events in smaller habitats.
worlds.visual_identity: Rotating cylinders, excavated rock, patched pressure structures and warehouses full of inbound necessities.

worlds.name: Bradbury Prime

environment.surface: cool plateaus, deep valleys and dry inland basins

settlement.reason_founded: Stable environment and isolation suitable for observatories and research.
settlement.why_remain: Universities, laboratories and precision industries accumulated around the original institutes.
settlement.character: Research campuses grew into cities.

culture: Cargo paperwork can be more demanding than customs because experiments impose exact handling requirements.
Academic rivalries coexist with intensely practical freight dependence.
worlds.visual_identity: Clean industrial campuses, observatory fields, compact cities and specialized receiving facilities.

worlds.name: Pelagos

environment.surface: ocean with volcanic island chains
environment.habitability: excellent for Vey; good for humans

settlement.reason_founded: Rare environment comfortable to both Vey and humans plus rich marine biology.
settlement.why_remain: Food, pharmaceuticals and biological industry.
settlement.character: One of the symbolic successes of early joint settlement.

culture: Mixed Vey-human communities developed local customs not native to either homeworld.
Waterborne freight remains important beneath orbital logistics.
worlds.visual_identity: Volcanic islands, floating industrial districts, aquaculture fields, humid ports and orbital transfer craft.

worlds.name: Tidemark

environment.surface: almost continuous deep ocean

settlement.reason_founded: Valuable dissolved minerals and unusual biological chemistry.
settlement.why_remain: Extraction remains profitable despite severe logistics.
settlement.character: Settlements are machines that happen to contain neighborhoods.

culture: Weather forecasts are operational documents.
Permanent residents distinguish dozens of platform and sea-state conditions outsiders simply call storms.
worlds.visual_identity: Floating industrial platforms, wave barriers, tethered structures, heavy rain and almost no natural landing ground.

worlds.name: Foundry

environment.atmosphere: thin but usable with assistance; volcanic contaminants common
environment.surface: hot volcanic uplands and tectonic basins

settlement.reason_founded: Abundant geothermal energy and accessible industrial minerals.
settlement.why_remain: Extremely cheap process heat and mature underground factories.
settlement.character: Surface terminals are only loading mouths for a much larger world below.

culture: Waste heat is treated as a resource stream.
Surface architecture is deliberately disposable compared with protected subsurface plant.
worlds.visual_identity: Black rock, steam plumes, freight elevators, heat exchangers and illuminated shafts descending into factory districts.

worlds.name: Port Meridian

environment.surface: constructed station

settlement.reason_founded: Refueling point where several useful routes converged.
settlement.why_remain: Network effects: warehouses, repair skill, brokers and expedition services attract more traffic.
settlement.character: A truck stop that grew until it became a city.

culture: Crews measure parts of the station by old dock numbers rather than official district names.
Nobody agrees which bar was actually first.
worlds.visual_identity: Freight rings, mismatched additions, fuel farms, repair gantries, cheap hotels, illuminated signs and ships from every major manufacturer.

worlds.name: Talos

environment.atmosphere: thin breathable mix at low elevations; supplemental oxygen common
environment.surface: cold high desert, exposed mineral formations

settlement.reason_founded: Survey teams confirmed commercially exceptional rare-mineral deposits.
settlement.why_remain: The boom is still expanding and fortunes are being made supplying it.
settlement.character: Almost everything looks temporary even when plans call it permanent.

culture: Arrival dates function as social seniority.
Arguments about what Talos will become are more common than agreement about what it is.
worlds.visual_identity: Prefab habitats, excavation pits, dust, temporary roads, stacked freight, overloaded pads and construction lighting all night.

worlds.name: Waystation

environment.surface: constructed habitat attached to an airless minor body

settlement.reason_founded: Fuel cache and emergency service point on the outward route.
settlement.why_remain: Mechanics, pilots and businesses accumulated until leaving made less sense than staying.
settlement.character: Nobody planned a town; that is still visible in every corridor.

culture: Locals remember ships and captains by name.
Temporary structures acquire permanent nicknames long before official addresses.
worlds.visual_identity: Connected pressure modules, old fuel tanks, repair sheds, reused cargo containers and a small crowded dock.

worlds.name: Lastlight

environment.atmosphere: cold, thin but breathable with acclimation
environment.surface: rocky subpolar plains and low mountain chains

settlement.reason_founded: Survey base positioned to support exploration beyond the established network.
settlement.why_remain: Exploration, limited mining and the strategic value of being the last substantial supply point.
settlement.character: Civilization feels concentrated rather than absent: one small place contains almost everything available for light-years.

culture: Departures beyond the charted routes are noticed.
Survey crews leave records and messages because the next ship may be weeks away.
worlds.visual_identity: One illuminated settlement against dark open terrain, antenna fields, fuel tanks, expedition warehouses and a small landing field.

worlds.name: Lastlight Orbital

environment.surface: constructed station

settlement.reason_founded: Separate heavy freight and expedition staging from the limited surface field.
settlement.why_remain: Large ships need a transfer point and explorers need a final place to assemble loads.
settlement.character: The last busy radio traffic before silence.

worlds.visual_identity: Compact truss station, external cargo racks, fuel tanks, survey craft and a disproportionate number of antennas.
